issues.body: The document continues to publish `fleet.active_agents = len(live)` and per-repository active-agent counts. The new comment explicitly acknowledges that, because `max_concurrent_workers` is 1, N concurrent agents proves at least N accounts. This is therefore still a public fleet-composition disclosure, not merely an unrelated operational metric. The clone-invariance test misses it by returning the whole `fleet` object from fixtures with no live leases, so it only proves invariance at zero load. Under otherwise identical 1-account and 3-account fixtures with one and three live leases, respectively, the published documents differ and disclose the lower bound. Retaining a knowingly composition-revealing field makes the stated minimization incomplete.
issues.fix_hint: Remove or cardinality-minimize the public active-agent and per-repository active-agent counts, or narrow the claimed privacy property and public messaging with explicit maintainer approval. Add a non-vacuous clone-invariance test using valid live leases at each fleet size so the test exercises this known disclosure.
issues.title: Published active-agent count still leaks account-fleet composition

issues.body: The new footer says `no account identities or fleet counts are published`, but the payload and page still publish `fleet.active_agents` and repository/model active-agent counts. The generator's own new comment calls that value a lower bound on fleet size. This absolute public assurance is therefore factually false even under the change's documented assumptions.
issues.fix_hint: Do not make the absolute no-fleet-count claim while active-agent counts remain public. Either remove/minimize those counts as part of this change or use accurate wording that does not deny the known disclosure.
issues.title: Footer falsely states that no fleet counts are published

verdict.summary: The per-account rows and direct account census fields are removed soundly, and the new projections and self-tests are generally non-vacuous and fail closed. However, the change claims that the public surface no longer publishes fleet counts while deliberately retaining a value that directly exposes a lower bound on account-fleet size. That makes the privacy change incomplete and the new public-facing assurance false.
